The graph above shows the function $y=\operatorname{cot}⁡(Bx)+D,$ where $B$ and $D$ are constants. What is $B+D?$
feedback.worked_solution:
The period $T$ of the function is

$$
T=\frac{5\pi }{3}.
$$

The formula for the period $T$ of the function $y=A\operatorname{cot}⁡(Bx+C)+D$ is given by 

$$
T=\frac{\pi }{B}.
$$

Applying the formula of the period, we get

$$
\frac{5\pi }{3}=\frac{\pi }{B}\,⟹\,B=\frac{\pi }{(\frac{5\pi }{3})}=\frac{3}{5}.
$$

The parameter $D$ represents the vertical shift of the cotangent function. We see that the function has been translated by $\frac{12}{5}$ units down. Hence, $D=-\frac{12}{5}.$

Therefore, $B+D=\frac{3}{5}+(-\frac{12}{5})=-\frac{9}{5}.$

Finally, the equation of the curve is

$$
y=\operatorname{cot}⁡(\frac{3x}{5})-\frac{12}{5}.
$$
